Exogenous (dietary) lipid pathway. Chylomicrons transport triglycerides from the intestines to peripheral tissues.
Lipids are digested
and absorbed in the small intestines where chylomicron synthesis occurs on the template of apo B-48. Nascent chylomicrons are released into the
lymphatic system before entering circulation.
Mature chylomicrons are formed after receiving the full complement of apolipoproteins from HDL.
Lipids are made available to peripheral tissues by lipoprotein lipase mediated lipolysis ultimately forming a chylomicron remnant.
Removal
of chylomicron remnants occurs by LRP and LDL receptor in the liver.
